title: Unified credit allocations and granular overage priorities (PRD)
creator: Anika Shah
description: Problem statement: Customers with multi-product contracts want predictable invoice behavior when a plan's pooled credits are exhausted across multiple routes (generation, embeddings, fine-tuning). Current behavior uses a simple first-come fallback to overage pricing which causes surprising high-cost spikes and manual support escalations. Scope: propose a unified credit allocation model with weighted, per-route priority tiers and an invoice-level effective-rate calculation to make overage cheaper to reason about. This PRD covers product requirements, acceptance criteria, high-level UX flows for the Console, API contract changes for entitlements, and billing system acceptance tests. Out of scope: changes to core token metering logic and tax/invoicing format changes. Goals: 1) Reduce billing support tickets tied to unexpected overage by 60% for pilot customers. 2) Provide per-invoice visibility showing how credits and weights were applied and the computed effective per-token rate. 3) Allow customers and account admins to declare priority weights per route and one fallback pool (burst). 4) Ensure predictable accounting for reserved capacity (Dedicated) customers who also consume hosted credits.
acceptance_criteria: Credit allocation engine exposes an API to assign: primary credit pool, N weighted route priorities (weights sum >0), and a fallback burst pool. API documented in Console and SDKs.
When plan credits are exhausted on a route, the system consumes credits from other route pools according to configured weights; consumption order is deterministic and logged.

Billing system produces an invoice line for: base plan allocation, credits consumed per route, credits borrowed via weighted allocation (with source pool annotated), and overage charges applied to fallback pool. Each line includes quantity, unit price, and effective per-token rate.
Console UI includes a per-billing-window visualization: pool balances over time, borrow events (timestamped), and a simulated invoice preview given current usage patterns and weights.

Customers can set/modify route weights in the Console; changes are effective at the next billing window by default, with an optional immediate 'apply now' toggle for trial customers; change events are recorded in audit logs.

End-to-end test coverage: unit tests for allocation logic, integration tests that replay representative usage traces and assert resulting invoice lines and totals, and a customer acceptance test (CAT) with 2 pilot accounts demonstrating reduced surprise overage.

Migration/playbook for existing customers: safe defaults assigned (equal weights per route) and an opt-in migration flow with explanatory UI and recommended presets for common workloads (chat-first, embedding-first, balanced).

Performance requirement: allocation decision latency under 5ms p95 for synchronous metering paths; batched reconciliation jobs must complete within nightly billing window SLA and not exceed existing compute budgets.
Security: changes must not expose other tenants' usage; audit logs must include actor, timestamp, prior/after weight values. Security review required and sign-off recorded.
Metrics: define and instrument functions to measure percent of invoices with unexpected >10% overage vs forecast and track support ticket volume before/after rollout.
